# Regions and the Feel of Nations

## Principles

> status: ratified (D-0055, D-0059, D-0079)

Three ratified rules govern all geography. One: the plot moves hub-and-spoke through
complex geography — settle a base, work the surrounding troubles, migrate on. Two: the
environment is a character — regions differ in backstory, in separation from one
another, and in how their local Wyrd behaves, giving the characters real things to
learn and discover in each. Three: the world must feel like it holds multiple distinct
"nations" — not merely named map-areas but genuinely different places, signposted by
language (one region's tongue textured more like Greek, another's more like Latin, and
so on), clothing, food, music, and all the cultural stuff.

## The four-biome frame

> status: provisional (D-0081, D-0180)

The session's working map, adopted by continued building. (The four regions' NAMES
are now ratified — see "The ratified names" below; the placeholder labels in this
section survive only as descriptive glosses.) A continent roughly
Britain-plus-Northern-Europe in scale, sealed at its edges by permanent storm-wrack:
Under the single proof-system architecture, a region is a local axiom environment:
materials, weather, history, and damaged reciprocity change which premises are
available and which failure modes dominate. Regions do not grant element powers.

- **The chalk uplands ("Chalk-Spines")** — arid limestone plateaus where the Wyrd runs
  thin and controllable: the imperial core. Speech: a clipped, transactional register
  descended from the rulers' tongue (Latin/High-German texture). Dress: bleached
  linens, hard geometry, color regulated by rank. Food: preserved, measured,
  flavorless. Music: metronomic, glassy, passionless — clockwork made audible.
- **The drowned lowlands ("Drowned Parishes")** — peat bogs and flooded parishes
  under acidic fog; the agricultural and textile heartland, slowly sinking. Speech:
  breathy, vowel-heavy, water-over-stones (Brythonic/Gaelic texture). Dress: oiled
  wool, reed-cloak, wax. Food: eel, tuber, bitter herb. Music: slow fiddle and frame
  drum — the sound this show's own score leans on.
- **The industrial crags ("Slag-Peaks")** — strip-mined mountains, soot air, violent
  hot-tempered Wyrd. Speech: guttural, percussive, forge-shouted (Norse/Slavic
  texture). Dress: hide, patchwork leather, iron clasps. Food: hardtack, cured fat,
  mine-fungus. Music: anvil percussion and throat-song.
- **The salt fringes ("Salt-Fringes")** — eroded coasts and stilt-villages under
  erratic sea-storms. Speech: rapid, melodic, whistled across water (Hellenic/
  Finno-Ugric texture). Dress: fish-leather and sailcloth sewn with thousands of
  micro-knots. Food: brine, kelp, gull-egg. Music: bone-flute, hurdy-gurdy, tuned
  wind-chimes turning gales into melody.

## Trio origins across the map

> status: provisional (D-0080, D-0081)

The ratified rule: the three come from three different regions, each origin strongly
dramatically justified. The provisional assignment: the protagonist from the chalk
uplands (raised above the rot, fluent in the rulers' clean arithmetic, physically
helpless in mud — her arc is a descent into the world her class abstracted away); the
apprentice from the salt fringes (a culture of flexible knots and fluid categories,
where rigidity drowns — survival by bending, which is also who they are); the anchor
from the industrial crags (iron, weight, dark tunnels, and the bill the body pays —
the working-class bedrock under the trio's feet).

## Earlier region sketches

> status: proposed

From the first session, unreconciled with the four-biome frame: a petrified
crystalline forest where sound itself is dangerous ("Glass Weald"); a fog-drowned
valley that eats short-term memory (also called "Drowned Parishes" — note the name
collision with the biome above AND with the narrator's woven chronicle; at most one
keeps the name); a de-mineralized wasteland where iron misbehaves ("Rust Wastes").
Each models the ratified principle of region-as-character with its own broken rule to
learn. Their canonical role is now settled (D-0119): these are anomaly deep-zones inside the
biomes — extreme micro-regions reached later, never nations of their own (see "The map
shape"). The specific set-pieces and their names remain proposed.

## The ratified names

> status: ratified (D-0101, D-0108, D-0111)

The four regions are named: **Whitecombe** (the chalk uplands), **Corsbach** (the
drowned lowlands), **Swartby** (the industrial crags), and **Halspetra** (the salt
fringes). The starting spoke is the valley of **Gwern** (Welsh: alder-swamp —
switching from the earlier Ffynnonhen lean), and its hub settlement is **Trefpen**.
What remains unadopted is the map itself, not the names: adjacency, whether more
regions exist beyond the four, and the other regions' hubs (Q-0009).

## The map shape

> status: ratified (D-0119)

The map is four biome-nations in a core-and-ring arrangement (D-0119): the chalk core
(Whitecombe) high in the middle, with the drowned lowlands (Corsbach), the industrial crags
(Swartby), and the salt fringes (Halspetra) around it and the coast outermost, the whole
sealed by permanent storm-wrack. The first hub is the lowlands valley of Gwern (hub Trefpen);
the party migrates outward and the arc ends at the chalk core — Moses returning to where she
began, so the migration order itself encodes the macro-arc (sabotage the periphery, then
breach the core, [[structure]]). Beneath it all runs a single downstream watershed:
extraction flows crags → lowlands → fringes, and the debt is made visible as water pushed
downhill ([[pre-history]]). For a multi-hundred-episode run each biome-nation may hold two or
three sub-nations of its own (D-0051); the finer adjacency and the other regions' hubs are
drawn as the spokes are written, not fixed here.
